text:
Daily life of a vibe-coder.

Me: Claude, why did you add this here? 
Claude: It's written in the implementation plan! 
Me: But why is it there? You're the one who created it! 
Claude: It's in the Acceptance Criteria. See? 
Me: Damn, right. But where did it come from? 
Claude: Well, from the requirements doc and PRD you gave me. Look, it's written here and here?
Me: Crap. The main thing in any investigation is not to trace it back to yourself 😅. Let's rewrite the requirements, make a PRD, break it down into User Stories and Acceptance Criteria, create an implementation plan. Anyway, 2 days of work down the drain.

After 6 months, I've learned to ship projects to release purely through vibe-coding. But I still can't accept: without specs, expect wrecks - even with humans, and with AI it's 10x worse. AI won't set itself up for success.

The irony is that I had to transform from an engineer into a product manager. Seems like the future belongs to product managers - they'll be in crazy demand.

Has anyone managed to build and maintain long-term projects through vibe-coding? Share your experience!
